level1.text: A stone is at rest high up on a cliff, and its potential energy is $50\,\text{J}$. The stone falls to the ground, where the potential energy is zero. Air resistance is ignored. What is the kinetic energy of the stone just before it hits the ground?

A plant leaf absorbs radiant energy of $245\,\text{J}$ from the Sun. Through photosynthesis the leaf changes $6.0\,\text{J}$ of it into chemical energy, and the rest changes into thermal energy. How much energy is changed into thermal energy?

A skater starts from rest at point A on the rim of a half-pipe and slides down a slope with friction, past point B, to point C at the bottom. The bars in the figure show his potential energy and kinetic energy at each point, with the bottom as the zero level of potential energy.

Read the energies from the figure. How much energy has friction changed into thermal energy when the skater has moved from point A to point C?

In each situation, name the form of energy that the energy is in at the start and the useful form of energy that it changes into. a) Firewood burns in a fireplace and warms a room. b) A solar panel produces electricity. c) Water flows down from a reservoir into a turbine that turns a generator.
level1.answer: a) chemical energy → thermal energy; b) radiant energy → electrical energy; c) potential energy of water → (kinetic energy →) electrical energy

level1.text: A sledge starts from rest at the top of a hill. At the top its potential energy is $600\,\text{J}$, and on the way down friction changes $90\,\text{J}$ of energy into thermal energy. At the bottom of the hill the potential energy is zero. What is the kinetic energy of the sledge at the bottom of the hill?
A charged phone is on a table and is not being used. What form of energy is the energy stored in the battery of the phone?

choices.feedback: Correct: the energy is stored in the battery chemically, in the chemical bonds between substances. When the phone is used, the chemical energy first changes into electrical energy and then into, for example, light and thermal energy.
Kinetic energy belongs to a moving object. A phone at rest on a table does not move, and the energy stored in the battery is not motion; the energy is bound in the substances of the battery.

Radiant energy is the energy of light and other electromagnetic radiation. In a battery the energy is not in the form of radiation but in chemical bonds; radiation is produced only when the screen of the phone starts to light up.

Potential energy depends on the height of an object relative to the zero level, like a ball at the edge of a cliff. The energy of the phone battery does not depend on how high the table is, but on the chemical bonds of the substances in the battery.

level1.text: A car drives along a level road and brakes to a stop. Which of the following describes correctly what happens to the kinetic energy of the car?
level1.answer: The kinetic energy changes into thermal energy in the brakes, the tyres and the road, and the total amount of energy stays the same.

choices.text: The kinetic energy changes into thermal energy in the brakes, the tyres and the road, and the total amount of energy stays the same.
choices.feedback: Correct: when braking, friction changes the kinetic energy into thermal energy, so the brakes, the tyres and the road warm up a little. Energy is not lost; it changes form.

choices.text: The kinetic energy disappears, because the car stops.
choices.feedback: Energy does not disappear. By the law of conservation of energy it only changes form or moves, and here the kinetic energy changes into thermal energy.

choices.text: The kinetic energy changes into thermal energy in the brakes, but the total energy decreases, because the heat is transferred to the surroundings.
choices.feedback: The surroundings are part of the system, so heat transferred to the surroundings does not disappear anywhere. By the law of conservation of energy the total energy stays the same: the kinetic energy has changed into thermal energy, which is in the brakes, the tyres, the road and the air.

choices.text: The kinetic energy is still in the car as kinetic energy, even though the car has stopped.
choices.feedback: A car that has stopped has no kinetic energy, because it is not moving. However, the energy has not disappeared; it is in the brakes, the tyres and the road as thermal energy.

level1.text: A phone is being charged with a charger from a wall socket, and the charger feels warm in the hand. Describe the change of energy as a chain, from the energy coming along the cable from the wall socket to the moment it is in the battery. Use the law of conservation of energy to explain why the charger warms up.
level1.answer: Electrical energy → (in the charger) electrical energy and thermal energy → chemical energy in the battery; part changes into thermal energy, so the charger warms up, and energy is not lost

level1.text: A ball is dropped from rest from a height of $1\,\text{m}$ onto a hard floor. It bounces several times, each bounce lower than the one before, and finally the ball comes to rest on the floor. The ball, the floor and the air are assumed to form an isolated system. Decide which statements about the situation are true and which are false.

statements.text: The mechanical energy of the ball after the first bounce is less than at the moment it was dropped.
statements.feedback: Correct: part of the mechanical energy of the ball changed into thermal energy in the collision and because of air resistance, so the mechanical energy $E_\text{p} + E_\text{k}$ decreased.

statements.text: The energy of the ball has been used up when the ball has stopped on the floor.
statements.feedback: Wrong: this is the misconception "energy gets used up". Energy does not disappear; it has changed into a form that is hard to use: the ball, the floor and the air have warmed up slightly.

statements.text: During the bounces the total energy of the ball, the floor and the air stays the same.
statements.feedback: Correct: the ball, the floor and the air form an approximately isolated system, so the sum of all forms of energy is the same at the start and at the end: $E_\text{initial} = E_\text{final}$.

statements.text: When the ball hits the floor, part of the energy changes into thermal energy, and so there is less energy in total than at the start.
statements.feedback: Wrong: thermal energy is part of the total energy. The mechanical energy decreases, but the total energy does not, because it only changes form.

statements.text: When the ball has stopped, its initial potential energy is thermal energy in the ball, the floor and the air.
statements.feedback: Correct: during the bounces the potential energy changed through kinetic energy into thermal energy, which is now in the ball, the floor and the air. It can no longer easily be used to lift the ball.

level1.text:
A kettle changes electrical energy into thermal energy; assume that all of the electrical energy goes into the water and no heat escapes to the surroundings. The kettle holds $0.50\,\text{kg}$ of water whose temperature rises from $20\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ to $60\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. The increase in the thermal energy of the water is $E = c\,m\,\Delta T$, where $c$ is the specific heat capacity of water, $m$ the mass and $\Delta T$ the change in temperature.

Look up the specific heat capacity of water in the MAFY table (mafytaulukot.fi). Hint: the value is in the thermodynamics table of specific heat capacities, on the row for water. How much electrical energy does the kettle change into thermal energy?

level2.text: An electric scooter sets off. Chemical energy of $3.00\,\text{kJ}$ is released from its battery, and the scooter and rider gain kinetic energy of $2150\,\text{J}$ from it. The rest changes into thermal energy in the battery, the motor and the tyres. How many joules of energy are changed into thermal energy?

A child starts from rest at the top of a water slide. At the bottom her kinetic energy is $2400\,\text{J}$, and on the way friction has changed $0.60\,\text{kJ}$ of energy into thermal energy. The bottom is the zero level of potential energy. What was the potential energy of the child at the top? Answer in kilojoules.

A child sitting on a swing is pulled to the side and released from rest. At the highest point the potential energy of the child and the swing is $0.36\,\text{kJ}$, when the zero level is the lowest point of the swing. The swing keeps swinging in smaller and smaller swings until it stops at the lowest point. Sound is ignored. How many joules of energy are changed into thermal energy in total?

Electrical energy of $360\,\text{kJ}$ goes into a kettle. Of this, $331\,\text{kJ}$ is transferred to the water as heat, and the rest warms the kettle and the surroundings. How many joules of energy end up in the kettle and the surroundings?

level2.text:
An inventor demonstrates a water device that he claims works forever without outside energy.

Water falling from the upper pool turns a generator and loses potential energy of $100\,\text{J}$ per cycle. The generator changes all of this energy into electrical energy. A pump uses $80\,\text{J}$ of it and lifts the water back to the upper pool, and the rest of the electrical energy goes to a lamp.

How many joules of energy does the device create from nothing in one cycle, if the claim is true? Explain which principle of energy is broken.

The table gives, as example figures, the electrical energy taken by three lamps in one hour and how much of it changes into light; for comparison, the lamps take the same electrical energy. The rest of the energy changes into thermal energy. How many kilojoules more thermal energy does the incandescent lamp produce than the LED lamp? Justify which lamp is the wiser one to use in terms of energy.

data.caption: Electrical energy of the lamps and the energy that changes into light in an hour

level2.text:
A skater starts from rest at point A on the rim of a half-pipe and slides down a slope with friction, past point B, to point C at the bottom. The bars in the figure show his potential energy and kinetic energy at each point, with the bottom as the zero level of potential energy.

Read the energies from the figure. What percentage of the skater's initial energy has friction changed into thermal energy by the time he reaches point B?

level3.text:
The energies of a skateboarder are measured at three points in a half-pipe.

At point A the skateboarder is at rest and her potential energy is $900\,\text{J}$. At point B the potential energy is $400\,\text{J}$ and the kinetic energy $480\,\text{J}$. At point C the potential energy is zero and the kinetic energy $750\,\text{J}$. Friction keeps changing mechanical energy into thermal energy.

How much energy is changed into thermal energy between points B and C?

A rubber ball is dropped on the floor. The mechanical energy of the ball is $5.00\,\text{J}$ when dropped, $4.00\,\text{J}$ after the first bounce and $3.20\,\text{J}$ after the second bounce. How much more energy is changed into thermal energy in the first bounce than in the second?

In a nuclear power plant, the nuclear reactions in the reactor heat water into steam, the steam turns a turbine and the turbine turns a generator, which produces electricity. The steam leaving the turbine is cooled with seawater, which warms up.

a) Name the forms of energy at each stage of the chain.

b) The plant turns only about a third of the nuclear energy released in the reactor into electrical energy. Use the law of conservation of energy to explain where the rest of the energy goes and why it has not been lost.
level3.answer: a) nuclear energy → thermal energy → kinetic energy of steam and turbine → electrical energy; b) about two thirds ends up as thermal energy in the sea and the surroundings, and the total energy is conserved

level3.text:
The table gives the total yearly energy consumption of an imaginary country by source (rounded example figures, not the statistics of a real country). The country has $5.5 \cdot 10^{6}$ inhabitants. Oil, coal and natural gas are fossil fuels.

a) Calculate the share of fossil fuels in the total consumption as a percentage.

b) Calculate the total consumption per inhabitant in gigajoules; $1\,\text{PJ} = 10^{15}\,\text{J}$ and $1\,\text{GJ} = 10^{9}\,\text{J}$.

c) The country wants to bring the share of fossil fuels below a third of the total consumption by replacing part of the fossil energy with hydro and wind power. The total consumption stays the same. At least how many petajoules of fossil energy must be replaced? Justify with a calculation and use the law of conservation of energy to explain why the total consumption can stay the same.

level3.text:
The LED lamp on a desk gets its electricity from a solar panel and a battery. The table gives the energies of one day at the stages of the chain: the input of each stage and the useful energy that goes on from it. The input of the next stage is the useful energy of the previous stage. The model assumes that the rest of the energy of a stage changes into thermal energy.

a) Calculate the energy that changes into thermal energy at each stage and in the whole chain in total.

b) At which stage is the most thermal energy produced, and what percentage of all the thermal energy is that?

c) Check the result with the law of conservation of energy and explain why the radiant energy arriving at the panel has not been used up, even though the light of the lamp is only a small part of it.
